h1: The Rim Riverside Guest House — a budget Mekong guesthouse where the owner treats you like family
intro: If you're doing Nong Khai on a budget but still want a Mekong riverside spot right in the Tha Sadet Market area, The Rim Riverside Guest House is a small, affordable guesthouse that reviewers mention two things about first: an owner who looks after guests personally, and the Mekong view from the upstairs rooms. It's an easy walk to Tha Sadet Market and the riverfront. Real guest reviews give it 4.3/5 on TripAdvisor (#3 of the specialty lodgings in Nong Khai) and 6.9 on Trip.com. Rooms from approx. ฿500/night.

body.html: The first thing guests mention here isn't the rooms or the facilities — it's the owner. Reviews describe him (foreign guests call him Mr Tung) as a genuinely kindhearted gentleman whose top priority is making guests comfortable, and who'll go out of his way to help — one review tells of him driving a guest to a currency exchange himself. That's the kind of family-run warmth a big hotel simply can't offer.

The second thing is the Mekong view. The guesthouse sits on the riverbank in the Tha Sadet Market area, and several upstairs rooms look straight out at the river and the Laos side. Older reviews call the view fabulous, especially from the upper floor. One honest caveat, though: a recent review warns that new construction has gone up between the guesthouse and the river, so some Superior rooms booked specifically for the river view no longer see the Mekong the way the online photos suggest. If you're booking for the view, message the property first to confirm your room still has an open outlook.
"Great location on the river, close to the main Nong Khai sights, the owner is friendly and so helpful, the room was clean and the river view from upstairs is genuinely fabulous."

There are only a handful of rooms — a downstairs Standard, an upstairs Superior, and a Queen Room with a balcony. Reviews that praise the rooms call them clean, more spacious than expected and well kept, with air-con, a fridge, hot water and Wi-Fi that actually works. The upstairs rooms are the best value because of the river view, but you trade that for fairly steep stairs — worth noting if you struggle with stairs or have heavy luggage.

Another nice touch is the small in-house cafe and backyard garden. A few tables sit out in the garden, and the cafe serves coffee and snacks that reviewers rate well — a relaxed spot for a morning or evening sit-down. There's bike hire for riding along the river, free parking and luggage storage. Just note that there is no breakfast on site, so you'll head out to eat — and the Tha Sadet Market area has plenty of riverside food to choose from anyway.

The location is a real strength. It's in the Tha Sadet Market area right on the Mekong, within walking distance of the market and the riverside restaurants, and close to the town's temples and main sights. One thing to accept from the reviews: the riverside road carries motorbike traffic in spells, so rooms facing the street can pick up some noise. The Thai–Lao Friendship Bridge is a short drive away, making this a handy base if you're crossing over to Vientiane.

The honest verdict: The Rim Riverside Guest House suits budget travellers and couples who value a riverside location and personal service over newness or a full facility list. For around ฿500–฿800 you get a clean room, an attentive owner and a walk to Tha Sadet Market — that's good value. But if you want a brand-new room, breakfast on site, or a guaranteed unobstructed river view, step up to a higher-tier riverside hotel.

A tip from reading the reviews: choose an upstairs room for the river view, but message the property first to confirm the outlook is still open after the new riverside construction. If stairs are an issue, ask for a downstairs room instead. The cool season (Nov–Jan) is Nong Khai's high season — rooms are few and fill fast, so book ahead and pick a free-cancellation rate just in case.

faqTitle: FAQ — The Rim Riverside Guest House Nong Khai

faq.q: Where is The Rim Riverside Guest House in Nong Khai, and what's nearby?
faq.a: It sits on the Mekong in the Tha Sadet Market area, on Takay Road in central Nong Khai. It's a few minutes' walk to Tha Sadet Market and the riverside restaurants. The Thai–Lao Friendship Bridge is about 3 km away and Nong Khai Railway Station roughly a 10-minute drive.

faq.q: How much does The Rim Riverside Guest House cost, and what room types are there?
faq.a: Rooms start at around ฿500/night for the downstairs Standard. There's an upstairs Superior with the river view and a Queen Room with a balcony, rising to around ฿800. Prices vary by season — always compare across platforms before booking.

faq.q: Do The Rim Riverside Guest House rooms still have a Mekong view?
faq.a: The upstairs rooms originally had a lovely river view, but a recent review warns that new construction on the bank now blocks the view from some Superior rooms. If you're booking for the view, message the property first to confirm your room still sees the open Mekong.

faq.q: Who is The Rim Riverside Guest House best for?
faq.a: It's great for budget travellers, couples, and anyone who wants a Mekong riverside spot in the Tha Sadet Market area with friendly, personal service. The owner looks after guests himself. If you want a brand-new room, breakfast on site, or a lift, step up to a higher-tier riverside hotel.

faq.q: Does The Rim Riverside Guest House serve breakfast?
faq.a: No breakfast is served on site, but there's a small in-house cafe serving coffee and snacks, and it's right by Tha Sadet Market, which has plenty of riverside food from early morning — an easy walk out for breakfast.

faq.q: What facilities does The Rim Riverside Guest House offer?
faq.a: It has an in-house cafe, a backyard garden, bike hire, free parking, luggage storage, free Wi-Fi and taxi booking. The owner helps with travel tips and crossing to Vientiane, making it a handy base if you're using Nong Khai as a gateway into Laos.
